motion.name: screen-enter
motion.value: opacity 0 and translateY(14px) to rest, 0.28s ease-out
motion.purpose: Every new screen; none on a redraw of the same screen, none on the light screen, none with reduced motion.

motion.name: line-draw
motion.purpose: A place line drawn in; continues from where it was on redraw; complete with reduced motion.

motion.name: line-reach
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset, linear, over the remaining seconds
motion.purpose: The other place's line reaching across on an invitation.

motion.name: button-pulse
motion.value: 1.6s ease-in-out infinite, cap to opacity .55 and scale .9 at 50%
motion.purpose: A press is expected; in step with the button's green light; off with reduced motion.

motion.name: ring-empty
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 0 to circumference, linear, over the remaining seconds
motion.purpose: Time running out; runs with reduced motion because it is information.

motion.name: number-pop
motion.value: scale 1.18 and opacity 0 to rest, 0.9s ease-out (0.8s for LIVE)
motion.purpose: Countdown number and LIVE word arriving.

motion.name: page-nudge
motion.purpose: The page counter on a consent notice when agreeing is pressed before the last page.

narrative.overview:
The booth screen is a black field on which places are drawn, not described. Each booth owns one continuous white or grey line built from copies of MIDAP's own mark, and every encounter the booth makes is told as two lines approaching, crossing and knotting. Type is Inter, large and few: one message per screen in German, with at most one short English line where a visitor needs it to act (ADR-040).

The density is that of a sign read from a metre away, not of an interface. Most of the canvas is empty black; one hero sentence sits top left, the drawn line runs through the middle, and the round button sits bottom left on every screen where a press is possible. The only departure from black is the countdown and flash, where the whole screen turns white because it is the light for the photo.

The screen refuses the photo-booth default of a camera frame, stickers and a big "take a photo" button. It has no colour, no glow, no fills on the line, no icons and no imagery other than the visitor's finished strip.
keyCharacteristics: Black ground, white type, one grey for the other place and for secondary text.
Inter only, from a heavy 128 px hero down to a 36 px floor (18 px on the panel).
One continuous stroke per place, MIDAP's mark repeated, one weight, round caps.
The physical round button drawn as a circle in a fixed place, bottom left.
Motion that draws and counts: lines drawn in, a pulse asking for a press, a ring emptying as time runs out.

rules.name: The Here-and-Elsewhere Rule
rules.body: White is this booth, grey is the other place. A line, label or mark belonging to another booth is always grey; this booth's is always white. No third hue is introduced to distinguish places; places are told apart by their name and their line's shape.

rules.name: The Word-Not-Colour Rule
rules.body: State is said in words, by symbol, or by the line and the ring, never by colour. There is no red, green or accent anywhere on the screen.

rules.name: The Arm's-Length Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing a visitor reads is smaller than 36 px on the canvas, 18 px on the panel (ADR-038). Operator-only text is the only exception.

rules.name: The One-Message Rule
rules.body: Each screen carries one German message and at most one short English line, and only where the visitor needs it to act (ADR-040). A second sentence, caption or label that repeats what the line, the light or the button already says is removed, not made smaller.

rules.name: The Over-Under Rule
rules.body: The only depth on the screen is a line passing over another at a real crossing. Nothing is lifted, shadowed or glowed.

dos: Do set every size on the 2560 x 1600 canvas and keep visitor text at 36 px or more (18 px on the panel).
Do draw the other place as a grey line labelled with its name, and this booth as a white line; let the line be the progress wherever something is being made.
Do put the round button bottom left at the 112 px margin, with one word beside it, on every screen that takes a press.
Do say time running out with the emptying ring, and time remaining in words ("Noch etwa eine Minute."), never with an elapsed clock.
Do turn the screen fully white, without a fade, while the camera needs light.
Do use tabular figures for every number that counts or must be copied.
donts: Don't add colour, glow, fills, gradients or shadows to anything the screen draws; the visitor's finished strip is the only image and the only colour, and the over-under gap at a real crossing is the only depth.
Don't draw a line from computed loops or any curve that is not MIDAP's mark or a smooth join between copies of it.
Don't show a camera frame, stickers or a "take a photo" button.
Don't add a second sentence, a caption or a label that repeats what the line, light or button already says.
Don't show the header bar, MIDAP's mark or a line on consent, countdown or flash screens.
Don't invent the funding notice or a placeholder for it.
